correctness.summary: The DFS-tree comparability property forces every complete-bipartite DFS tree into an alternating spine with any surplus vertices attached as same-side leaves at the terminal spine vertex. Exact cut counts give the h_i and g_i profiles; leaf-envelope loads are dominated by a spine cut, the larger-part root is optimal, and neighboring-profile comparisons reduce the optimum to one concave quadratic except for the balanced odd parity correction. Complete graphs force Hamilton-path DFS trees and have cut load i(n-i)-1. Definition-level finite checks agree with all formulas tested.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The current Bourotte--Ducloz--Orponen--Seki paper defines KLX and DTC and develops small-KLX structure, treewidth bounds, and recognition, but the inspected full text contains no exact clique or complete-bipartite formula. Searches under KLX, kissing-loop crossing, DFS-tree congestion, Trémaux-tree congestion, and related formulations found no equivalent result. Classical spanning-tree-congestion results for complete multipartite graphs optimize over arbitrary spanning trees and do not imply these DFS-restricted formulas. Very recent unindexed work and older terminology remain residual risks.

value.summary: The result gives exact KLX and DTC values on two fundamental dense graph families. The biclique formula identifies a sharp balance-to-imbalance phase transition, and comparison with ordinary spanning-tree congestion shows an asymptotically linear penalty for requiring a DFS tree on cliques and balanced bicliques.

limitations: The theorem does not cover general complete multipartite graphs.
It does not classify all KLX-minimizing ordered DFS trees.
No stability result is proved for nearly complete graphs or bicliques with deleted edges.
Very recent unindexed KLX work and older literature under substantially different terminology remain residual originality risks.
Finite computation supports but does not replace the proof.
Independent audit has not been performed.
